description.narrative: After Storm Daniel struck Libya on Sep 10, with over 5000 presumed dead and 10000 still missing. While rescue teams are actively searching for survivors, the widespread displacement is evident, especially in Derna and around Benghazi, where data indicates over 30000 newly displaced individuals. While local and national authorities are leading the work on the ground, they are overwhelmed by the scale of the disaster, as around 884000 people in five provinces have been directly affected by the storm and flash floods, with varying degrees of impact. OCHA stresses the need for emergency shelter, relief items like tarps, blankets, solar lamps, and psychosocial support as well as food security and WASH. Hospitals are strained, treating both storm victims and their own affected staff, demanding urgent healthcare services. Benghazi faces escalating challenges due to an influx of internally displaced persons, and Al Bayda is also heavily affected.

DCA's response is rooted in inclusivity and a determination to reach all affected HHs, regardless of age, gender, religion, or ethnicity. It recognizes the diverse needs and vulnerabilities within the affected communities. Most of the response will be targeting IDPs who have left the affected areas to seek shelter in schools, public structures, or HCs. We expect that 90% of our beneficiaries will be IDPs and consider 10% of the budget for HC support as well. The first phase of emergency NFIs distribution aims at supporting emergency specific displacement related needs, the phase of MPCA will allow recipients to meet other basic needs, in an empowered and dignified manner. Vulnerable groups include female-headed HHs, HHs with individuals with disabilities or specific needs, pregnant and lactating women, and elderly. DCA will be sensitizing selection committees on inclusivity, facilitating access at distribution sites and coordinating with other actors and creating referral mechanisms.

Together with Dan Church Aid (DCA), an ACT Alliance member, Cordaid will focus on two sectors:
1. NFIs: Distributing NFI kits, prioritizing IDPs. Based on cluster standards, local customs, and coordination with the LRC and authorities, kits’ composition will be Solar lamp, Mattress, Floor mats, Blankets, Towels, Kitchen kits, curtains (for privacy), and necessary hygiene items. The overall kit value will be 200 EUR. Focus will be on the displaced households that have fled the affected areas, as they are amongst the most vulnerable right now. DCA expects to support 700 displaced households (4200 individuals).
2. Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA): To cater for the emergency multi-sector needs of the storm-affected population: two-month MPCA to enable households to meet their basic needs. 375 IDP and host community households (2,250 individuals) will receive 181 EUR twice, which is based on the current full MEB value (CWG April 2023). The transfer value may be revised in coordination with the Cash and Market Working group and other clusters. DCA will work with CSOs to identify the most affected and vulnerable households.

description.narrative: Unconditional transfers are provided to beneficiaries without the recipient having to do anything in return in order to receive the assistance . Unrestricted transfers can be used entirely as the recipient chooses i.e. there are no restrictions on how the transfer is spent (Definitions of CALP). It can be delivered e.g. through local banks, shops, traders, local money transfer companies, remittance companies and post offices in either one or several instalments.

SPHERE: Communities and people affected by crisis, including the most vulnerable groups, consider that the timing of the assistance and protection they receive is adequate. DRA: timely depends on the nature of the acute crisis (slow versus sudden onset). If it is an acute sudden onset crisis a response is considered timely if we decide to respond within 48 hours and if we initiate the response within 72 hours. If it is a slow onset crisis, it is timely if we initiate the response in 3 weeks after we decide that the crisis meets the criteria of an acute crisis.
The applicable definition depends on the type of crisis (protracted versus acute). The SPHERE definition should be used in more protracted crisis where there is (more) time to conduct assessments and measure satisfaction of the response in the eyes of people affected. The DRA definition should be used for acute crises, where it is more important to initiate the response as soon as possible and look at our own processes.
